why: Pushing e5 put an undefended pawn where the Nf3 attacks it, instead of removing the pinning bishop's partner first with Bxf3.
With the king on h1 and black queen on h3, the Nf3 idea threatens mate, and f5 ignored it instead of f3.
Rg1+ with Bg7+ discoveries was coming, and b5 did nothing about it while Kh8 stopped it.
Taking the pawn on d6 ignored the Nf3 and Qh3 threats against the king and left the pawn attacked three times.
Be3 stepped off the line and let a discovered attack win the queen on d6, instead of Qb3 dealing with the black queen.
Recapturing with the bishop (Bxc4) trades the right piece and develops it, whereas Nxc4 gave up the knight.
Ng4 would have gained time by attacking the bishop, while castling allowed Bb2 and Ndb5 with tempo.
Recapturing fxg3 damaged the pawn structure and the centre, where hxg3 kept the pawns intact and opened the rook.
11...h6 hits the queen with a pawn and wins the knight, whereas Bb4 wasted the move and left d5 loose.
d4 challenges the centre and attacks c5 and e5, which Bc3 left to Black.
Recapturing with the pawn (bxc6) keeps the bishop pair and solid structure, while Bxc6 allowed Nxe5.
The knight on f7 forks queen and rook, and Qe7 lost the rook on h8 instead of taking Bxf2+ first.
c6 attacks the rook on d5 with a pawn and gains time, where bxa5 let White's pawns and rook dominate.
The knight on g5 can be hit by h6, and Qf3 neglected that and lost time before a4 or retreating.
Recapturing with the knight keeps the better bishop and piece structure, whereas Bxd5 traded poorly.
